bull.b: EQT combines unusually strong margins with conservative leverage, giving it financial flexibility across the gas cycle. This foundation can support ongoing investment, debt management and shareholder returns while helping the company withstand periods of weaker commodity pricing.

Reliable operating cash generation and production outperformance indicate that EQT’s scale and execution are translating into tangible financial results. Drilling records, compression improvements and lower planned CapEx could reinforce productivity and sustain competitive cost performance.

Long-duration power and LNG agreements can diversify EQT’s sales exposure beyond spot Appalachian gas and create more visible future demand. These contracts may improve realized economics, support planning confidence and strengthen access to expanding domestic and international markets.

bear.b: EQT remains fundamentally tied to natural gas prices, regional differentials and market supply-demand conditions. Even with efficient operations, weaker prices can reduce revenue and cash generation, making earnings less predictable and limiting the durability of recent profitability.

The value of EQT’s contracted-demand strategy depends partly on infrastructure and customer projects that are years from completion. Delays could postpone expected cash flows, extend exposure to commodity markets and require continued capital spending before benefits are realized.

The proposed Range combination could add scale, but its benefits are not yet secured because regulatory and shareholder approvals remain outstanding. Closing conditions and subsequent integration create execution uncertainty that could delay synergies or increase management complexity.
